what_its_for: Azilsartan medoxomil is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults. Lowering your blood pressure helps reduce your risk of having a heart attack or stroke. This medicine works by relaxing your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard to pump blood.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Try to take it at the same time every day so it becomes part of your routine. Do not crush or split the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 80 mg once daily. Your doctor may start you on 40 mg once daily if you are taking certain water pills (diuretics like high-dose chlorthalidone). Your doctor will decide the right dose for you, so do not change your dose without talking to them first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it in the original container, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes that contain potassium unless your doctor tells you otherwise, as this medicine can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure further and make dizziness worse. Be careful when standing up quickly, especially in hot weather or after exercise, as this can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Do not take NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) regularly without checking with your doctor, as they can reduce how well this medicine works and harm your kidneys.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); dizziness or fainting; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness; decreased urination or signs of kidney problems; or if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. This drug can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby if taken during pregnancy.
when_it_works: You may start to see some blood pressure lowering within the first 1 to 2 weeks, but it can take up to 4 weeks to feel the full benefit. Keep taking this medicine every day even if you feel well. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious injury or death to your unborn baby. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and may have a higher risk of dizziness or falls. Kidney or liver disease: Use with caution. Your doctor may monitor you more closely or adjust your dose if needed. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in patients under 18 years of age.
